newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-LIG profit surge crowns recovery.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-LIG profit surge crowns recovery.

text.p: One of the world's biggest makers of condoms, London International Group Plc (LIG), announced a sharp rise in full-year profits on Thursday and told shareholders its three-year recovery programme was now complete.

LIG, which also makes rubber gloves for medical and domestic use, said pre-tax profits rose 12.6 percent to 29.5 million pounds ($48.3 million) after net restructuring charges of 6.1 million pounds and despite sterling's strength. Sales climbed to 339.2 million pounds from 309.6 million.

"This is the end of the recovery - we are back to where we should have been," ebullient chief executive Nick Hodges told Reuters. "London International is now entering a new phase of its development."
In a sign of renewed vigour the dividend was raised to 2.8 pence from 2.0 pence and Hodges promised "double- digit earnings growth for the next few years."
LIG shares responded with a rise of 11.5 pence to 168 pence, although they remained below a 12-month peak of 182 pence touched earlier this month and 1993 highs of well over 200 pence.
The company has climbed back from disaster in 1994, when it announced losses of 175 million pounds and a 115 million pound rights issue.

A series of bad diversifications in the 1980s as management panicked that its core businesses faced long-term decline led to ill-judged moves into businesses including photo-processing, saddling LIG with hefty restructuring charges and increasing trading losses.

Renewed interest in condoms and rubber gloves in the face of the AIDS threat and a strategy of selling-off non-core businesses helped LIG achieve its target of returning to pre-crash levels of profitability by the middle of 1997.
Profit margins also continued to progress towards the group's 15 percent target, improving to 12.3 percent from 10.1 percent a year earlier.

Hodges said the company would grow through further acquisitions and by winning "market share, new products and finding new users." LIG said it planned to raise its marketing budget by 20 percent in the current year to around 36 million sterling, mostly focused on its condom brands.

It also said it would roll out the world's first polyurethane condom, Avanti, worldwide. Avanti is sold at premium prices and LIG said it offered better sensitivity and overcame allergies to standard latex condoms.

LIG said it would use its strong cash flow to continue on the acquisition trail, adding to the U.S. Aladan glove and condom business, Portuguese glove maker Franco and Spanish condom brand Androtex bought in the last financial year.

Analysts welcomed the results which were in line with forecasts. Salomon Brothers analyst Jeremy Green said the only dark spot was the North American condom market where LIG is a distant number to Carter-Wallace Inc. LIG has been shedding brands to focus on the strong Durex name.
"That is a very sensible thing to do, but the price you pay is losing market share on an interim basis," Green said. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
